results.name: Rendering Thickness
results.title: Rendering Thickness
results.body:
Set the rendering thickness for the patterns.

Rendering thickness value is only visible and does not Simulate as the thickness value space out between Fabrics. 

  1. Select the pattern to set the rendering thickness.
    * To see the rendering thickness, 3D Garment Rendering Style must be set to one of the thick-surface styles.
     
  2. Set the thickness options in Property Editor.
    Option

    Description
    Add'l Thickness - Rendering

    Enter desired rendering thickness value.

    This value is for rendering purposes only and does not affect collisions. However, when exporting, enabling the Thick option will export both the Side and Back Mesh and UVs

    ✨Tip:Collision thickness can be adjusted at [Simation Properties ▶ Add'l Thickness - Collision]. 
    Extrusion Direction

    Specify the direction in which thickness is applied based on the Pattern Plane.

    Both

    Apply thickness evenly to both the front and back based on the Pattern.

    Forward

    Apply thickness forward.

    Backward

    Apply thickness backward.

    Toggle each side on or off to determine whether to generate the Mesh.

    Front Face

    Specify whether to generate the Front Face. 

    Back Face

    Specify whether to generate the Back Face. 

    Seam Face

    Specify whether to generate the surface where the stitched and bonded parts meet.
    Side Geometry

    Curvature (%)

    		 Specify the curvature.
    Resolution Set the number of subdivisions.
    Doubled Sided Apply the same curve to both sides.
    UV Expansion

     Watch Video

    The side and back UVs can be edited in UV Editor.

    Back Face

    Switch the UV from the front to the back.

    Side Face

    Expand the UVs to include the side.

results.name: Adjust Rendering Thickness
results.title: Adjust Rendering Thickness
results.body:
List of Contents

Fabric Unit

Pattern Unit

Objective 

Set Fabric thickness for a Garment in the 3D Garment window. Rendering thickness from the center of the Garment is set for 0.5mm as default vale, and it is adjustable. This thickness value is only visible and does not Simulate as the thickness value space out between Fabrics. 

※ Note: To see the rendering thickness, 3D Garment Rendering Style must be set on Thick Textured Surface .


Location

Fabric Unit

Object Browser ▶ Fabric ▶ Fabric Item ▶Property Editor ▶ Thickness 

Pattern Unit (ver2.3.0)

Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ Add'l Thickness-Rendering


Operation

Fabric Unit

  1. Follow the indicated guideline below:

    Object Browser ▶ Fabric ▶ Fabric Item ▶Property Editor ▶ Thickness

  2. Enter desired rendering thickness value. 
    →The thickness is now being adjusted and applied.

Pattern Unit (ver2.3.0)

  1. Follow the indicated guideline below:

    Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ Add'l Thickness-Rendering

  2. Enter desired rendering thickness value. 
    →The thickness is now being adjusted and applied.

Go back to the List of Contents

results.name: Adjust Collision Thickness
results.title: Adjust Collision Thickness
results.body:
Simulation thickness is invisible set property that represents the collision limit for Garments to result smooth Simulation.
 

📝 Note: For the same reason, the default value of Avatar thickness (Skin Offset) is set for 3mm. For form-fitting Garments or accurate fitting measurement, it is recommended that Skin Offset is adjusted alongside the Simulation thickness.

  1. Select Pattern in 2D/3D Window ▶ Property Editor ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ Add'l Thickness-Collision
     
  2. Enter desired rendering thickness value. 
    →The thickness is now being adjusted and applied.

 

Collision Thickness has been improved so that its thickness direction matches Rendering Thickness, ensuring that the visible thickness and simulation collision are applied consistently.

results.name: USD Layer Window
results.title: USD Layer Window
results.body:
New in 2025.0

Create/Open

Set Options

Export 

With USD, a graphics standard file format, you can increase collaboration productivity with a variety of 3D software. You can export clothing, avatars, and accessories with meshes and materials as USD files.  You can also import USD files created in other 3D software packages into CLO. A list of layers for the imported file can be found in the USD Layer window.
 

Create/Open

  1. Click Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ Display ▶ Windows ▶ USD Layer. 
     Or, right-click on the top of the side window, such as Object Browser or Property Editor.
    Create

    Create an USD file
    - An USD file is created with the specified path and name, appearing in the USD Layer window. This file will be set as the Authoring Layer.

    - When exporting the Material, a Texture folder is created within the directory where the USD is saved.
    Open Import an USD file
    Clear Delete all the layers listed in the USD Layer.

  2. The list of created or opend USD layers is structured as follows.  

    Authoring Layer

    The default layer which is being used at the moment.

    - When running Export to USD Layer for clothing, trims, scenes and props, they will be exported to the Authoring Layer.
    Material  The default path where the Materials appear.
    - Users can name this path while running Export to USD Layer.
    Mesh The default path where the Mesh appears.
    - Users can name this path while running Export to USD Layer.

Set Options

  1. Right-click on the layer list to set options if needed.

    Set Authoring Layer

    		 Set the selected layer as active. 
    - The same can be done by double clicking the left mouse button
    This menu won't appear in the following situations:
    - Where the selected layer is already set as the Authoring Layer.
    - Where the selected layer is an USDZ (read only)
    - Where the selected layer is missing.

    Delete

    		 Deleted the selected layer.
    This menu won't appear in the following situations:
    - Where the selected layer is the Authoring Layer.

    Export USDZ from Layer

    Export the selected layer as USDZ (read only)

    Once an USDZ is imported, it cannot be exported again.

Export

To export your cloth and/or trim assets from CLO as a USD file; select the assets from either 3D or 2D window, and click "Export to USD Layer" of the object context menu to export them to the Authoring Layer. This will update the USD file corresponding to the Authoring Layer.

  1. Set export options if needed.

    Prim

    Mesh

    		 Prim Path

    Either select or deselect Mesh.

    - You can name the Prim Path for the Mesh when exporting.

    Material

    		 Prim Path

    Either select or deselect Material.

    - You can name the Prim Path for the Material.

    - When exporting the Material, a Texture folder is created within the folder where the USD is saved. All related textures will be saved in that Texture folder. 
    Object

     

    Single Object

    Exports selected object as a single object.

    Multiple Objects

    Exports selected object as multiple objects.

    Thin

    Export USD without the rendering thickness.

    Thick

    Export USD with the rendering thickness as Geometry.

    Unified UV Coordinates

    Exports the texture data for all patterns to fit within UV coordinates
    Image Size

    Set the size of the image in pixels
    Fill Texture Seams

    Extend the scope of texture based on the texture's borders. 

    Include Garment Simulation Data

    		 USD export for garments, including the necessary data for simulation setup.

    Include Fur Strand Data

    Include the Fur Strand information.
    Option Cache Animation

    Saves pattern cache animation.

    📝Note: Since Pattern Cache Animation is exported as a mesh itself, there is no separate Animation Type prim.
    Avatar Animation
         		Joint

    Saves the animation data for Avatar animation as skeletal animation.

    Avatar Animation is exported to the USD Layer Window as a SkelAnimation type below SkelRoot.

    Cache

    Saves avatar cache animation.

    Basic

    Scale

    		 Set the unit of scale.

    %

    		 Adjust the scale in percentage.

    Axis Conversion

    Up Axis

    Select the up-axis used in the application where the file was imported from. Marvelous Designer will compare the up-axis of the incoming file and apply conversion if necessary.

    📝Note: In Marvelous Designer, the Y axis is the up-axis.

 

📝Note: When exporting garment using Export to USD Layer, the exported output will differ depending on the 3D Garment Rendering Style state. If the 3D garment appears in Thick Textured Surface, it will be exported with thickness.

results.name: Alembic Import/Export
results.title: Alembic Import/Export
results.body:
List of Contents

Import

Export 

Import/Export the object, cache, normal, and animation data contained within an Alembic file.

Import

  1. Click Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ Alembic.

  2. Select the desired file and click OK.

  3. Select the settings as needed and click OK.
    → The Alembic file is imported based on the setting.
    Option

    Description

    FPS

    Sets the frame rate of the cache data.
    Scale Input the scale directly or select from the available units.
    Garment Position Moves the Garment to the location of the first frame.

Export

  1. Click the Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ Alembic.
  2. Designate the file saving path and the file name. Then, click OK.
    → The Export Alembic window appears.
  3. Select the settings as needed and click OK.
    → The file is exported as an Alembic file based on the setting.
    Option

    Description

    File

    		 Set the file type (OGAWA/HDF5) for export.

    Object 

    Unweld

    Exports the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern

    that are sewn together into one line into multiple objects.

     Weld 

    Combines the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern

    that are sewn together into one line into one point.

    Weld Selected Pattern: Weld based on the sewing line that connects the selected patterns

    Thin

    Ensures that the thickness will not be exported even if the rendering thickness value is increased beforehand.

    Thick 

    Exports a pattern with its rendering thickness values in its increased state.

    Combined UV Coordinates: Exports all Garment Pattern texture data fit to UV Coordinates ranging from 0 to 1.

    Include Avatar Shape: Save the Avatar as part of the file.
    FPS

    Sets the frame rate of the cache data.
    Step

    Adds/Subtracts frames for the recorded Animation according to the entered value.
    Frame Relative Sample

    Sets the low and high values for frame relative sampling.
    Scale Adjusts the scale of the file being exported when a value is entered or the desired unit from “Unit in file to import” is selected.

results.name: Cache Animation Export
results.title: Cache Animation Export
results.body:
Objective

Export Animation cache data.

※ Note: You can export only the cache data of garments. 


Location

Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ Animation

  • Maya Cache (.mc)

  • Maya Cache (.mcx)

  • Point Cache 2

  • MDD Cache (Standard)

  • MDD Cache (Maya/3ds Max)


Operation

  1. Click the tool/menu indicated.
    → The Save File window appears.  

  2. Select the desired file and click OK.
    → The Export window opens.

  3. Set the full details and click OK.

     

    Object

    Unweld/Weld Object Export the selected objects as unweld or weld objects. 

    ※ Note: This option is removed from 6.2 and above. 

    Unweld

    Exports the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern

    that are sewn together into one line into multiple objects.

    ※ Thickness exports for quad meshes available beginning version.

    Weld 

    Combines the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern

    that are sewn together into one line into one point.

    Selected Pattern: Weld based on the sewing line that connects the selected patterns.

    Thin

    Ensures that the thickness will not be exported even if the rendering thickness value is increased beforehand.

    Thick 

    Exports a pattern with its rendering thickness values in its increased state.

    Combined UV Coordinates: Exports all Garment Pattern texture data fit UV Coordinates ranging from 0 to 1.

    ※Note: Unified Texture export multiple layers of texture information as a single UV texture information.
    Scale Adjusts the scale of the file being exported when a value is entered or the desired unit from Unit in file to import is selected.
    Axis Conversion Changes the directions of each axis of the object.
    Animation

    Entire Area (saves all of the recorded garment animation.)

    Play Area Only (saves only the play area garment animation.) 
    File

    Save With Texture Files (.zip): Exports the .obj file, .mtl file, and texture images used in the garment as one compressed file when exporting animation.

    Save with Meta Data (.xml) : Export the garment's pattern (Mesh), physical property, and sewing information as Meta Data (ver2.3.0).

    Diffuse Color Combined on Texture: Combine and save the garment's texture image and color as a single image (ver2.2.0).

    Exclude Ambient Color (for Modo): Exclude the Ambient color value when saving materials (ver2.2.0).

results.name: 3D Vertical Toggle Icons
results.title: 3D Vertical Toggle Icons
results.body:
Quality Render 

High-quality render is supported in the standard 3D Window.

 

Schematic Render 

Use this view to create tech pack images. Learn more here.

 

3D Garment Display/Hide

 

 Show Garment (Shift+C)

Show or hide garments.

Show Archived Pattern (Shift+C)

Show or hide archived pattern pieces.

Show 3D Seamlines (Shift+S)

Show or hide seamlines.

Show Internal Lines

Show or hide internal lines.

Show Baselines

Show or hide baselines.

Show Graphics

Show or hide graphics.

Show 3D Pen (Garment) 

Show or hide 3D pen markings on garments.

Show Threads 

Show or hide sewing lines connecting patterns.

Show Pins

Show or hide pins.

Show Garment Measurements

Show or hide garment measurements.

Show 2D Measurements

Show or hide measurements created with the POM tool.

 



 

Trim Display

  Show Button

Show or hide buttons and buttonholes

Show All Pipings

Show or hide pipings.

Show Bond/Skive

Show or hide bonding and skiving.

Show Puckering

Show or hide puckering.

Show All Trims

Show or hide any trims in the scene

 

Avatar Display

Show Avatar (Shift+A)

Show or hide avatars.

Show Arrangement Points (Shift+F)

Show or hide arrangement points.

Show Bounding Volumes

Show or hide bounding volumes.

Show Avatar Joints (Shift+X)

Show or hide IK joints.

Show Avatar Measures

Show or hide avatar measurements.

Show 3D Pen (Avatar)

Show or hide 3D pen markings on avatars.

Show Avatar Fitting Suit

Show or hide avatar fitting suits.

 

3D Garment Rendering Style

Thick Textured Surface (Alt+1)

View fabrics with any added thickness (fabric thickness of fabrics themselves and additional thickness - rendering of pattern pieces).

Textured Surface (Alt+2)

View fabrics without thickness.

Thick Monochrome Surface (Alt+3)

View fabrics without their maps/images and any added thickness (fabric thickness of fabrics themselves and additional thickness - rendering of pattern pieces).

Monochrome Surface (Alt+4)

View fabrics without their maps/images.

Translucent Surface (Alt+5)

Applies an amount of transparency to all fabrics.

Thick Textured Surface (Back)

The texture, graphic, and topstitches applied to the back of the garment are displayed instead of the front.

Random Color Surface (Alt+W)

Distinguish patterns easily due to randomly colored surfaces.

 

3D Garment Rendering Option

Show Wireframe (Alt+9)

View the mesh of fabrics and buttons.

Show Knitwear

Show or hide scene components which have the material type Knitwear applied.

Show Fur Strand

Show or hide scene components which have the material type Fur Strand applied.

Random Fur Strand Color

Randomize the color of individual fur strands.

 

Garment Fit Maps 

Stress Map (Alt+6)

Displays the force along the fabric grain per unit area (i.e. stress) applied to a garment through color codes and numerical values (kPa).

Strain Map (Alt+7)

Displays the stretch rate (i.e. strain), starting from 100% at zero strain, caused by external forces.

Fit Map (Alt+8)

Displays the tightness of a garment through color codes.

Show Pressure Map

Displays the external pressure exerted by garments onto avatars. (ver 7.3 )

 

Avatar Rendering Style

Textured Surface

Displays avatars with their respective maps/images.

Monochrome Surface

Displays any avatar surfaces in without maps/images.

Mesh

Displays the mesh structure of avatars.

 

Environment Display 

Show Light (3D) 

Displays the lights of the 3D window.

Show Light (Render)

Render-only light components appear in the 3D window.

Show Wind Controller

Displays any wind Controllers in the 3D window.

Show 3D Shadow

Displays shadows to the scene in the 3D window.

Show Ground Grid

Displays a 3D grid on the ground in 3D window.
Show Grid

Displays a 3x3 grid in the 3D Window.
